skill.name: copywriting
skill.description: Use when writing or rewriting marketing copy on a page — homepage, landing, pricing, features, about, or product — so the agent gathers audience and offer context before producing copy that converts.
whenToUse: Drafting hero, value prop, and CTA copy for a new landing page from scratch
Rewriting a weak page where the user says copy is unclear, generic, or not converting
Sharpening pricing, feature, or about copy so it persuades the right buyer
Producing headline and subheadline variations to A/B test against a current page

keyConcepts.explanation: Every page targets exactly one action — sign up, book a demo, buy. Copy that fights itself by promoting two primary actions doesn't convert either.
The skill insists on capturing how the customer describes their problem in their own words. Copy that mirrors the user's vocabulary outperforms clever copy almost every time.
Lead with the outcome the buyer gets, then back it up with the feature that delivers it. 'Hours of life back per week' beats 'Smart filter engine.'
Every persuasive claim should be paired with a number, testimonial, or case study within scroll distance. Unbacked claims read as marketing fluff.
Like the rest of this pack, copywriting reads .agents/product-marketing.md (or the legacy paths) before asking discovery questions, so the agent doesn't re-collect known business context.

gotchas: Don't write copy before you know the one primary action — the agent will produce hedging copy that converts neither path
If the user can't describe the customer's exact words, ask for support tickets or sales-call notes before drafting
Generic 'innovative, leading, scalable' adjectives are banned; replace them with a specific outcome or a number
Above-the-fold copy fights for attention with imagery; if a hero image is loud, the headline must be louder, not quieter
Email and popup copy use different patterns; route to the emails and popups skills for those surfaces
